answer: Reserve a fixed bond for every unresolved agent request, and release it only after the server finishes or a bounded timeout expires. A shared ledger prevents the same coins backing two requests. If falcon opens plume and cedar aliases, all three still compete for its finite collateral; new keys cannot multiply its queue slots. Flooding now ties up capital for the full service interval, while a timeout penalty pays for wasted capacity. This curbs simultaneous sybil traffic, not wealthy attackers or cheap repeated requests.
